subject: OptiDocs — Persistent rejections and elevated latency after burst-window change

Subject: Immediate: huge spike in 429s + 3x p95 after your config change

Hi Grace / Sean,

We started seeing a large spike in 429s and sustained p95 latency increases shortly after ~22:00 UTC last night. Metrics at our end: 429 rate hit 18% for a sustained 30m window, p95 token latency increased from ~120ms to ~380ms, and overall throughput fell ~40% for our production tenant (OptiDocs). This began right after the burst-window change you pushed (we were notified of the policy update).

Attached is a short ops dump (ops_dump_20260819.txt) showing request traces and timestamps. We also see repeated "quota_exceeded" responses that list a window mismatch; the body sometimes contains a 10s window token bucket error even though our contract indicates a 60s burst window.

This is customer-impacting; their production workflows are stalled and users are seeing timeouts. Can you confirm whether a change was deployed that modified burst/refill behaviour for our tier? We need an immediate mitigation plan.

Regards,
Alex Tan
Head of Platform Engineering — OptiDocs
OptiDocs, Inc.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-19T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick technical read on OptiDocs 429 spike (notes)

Team — quick summary after looking at the rollout logs and the attached traces:

What we changed: a policy adjustment to the global burst window enforcement shipped as part of the "burst harmonization" rollout. Default refill/windown was tightened in some rule paths from 60s->10s to reduce burst credit accumulation for large tenants. The config accidentally matched OptiDocs' tenant id in the rollout flag evaluation (edge case in policy targeting).

Why this impacted OptiDocs: their bursty traffic pattern relies on a 60s smoothing window; the 10s window collapses effective burst credits and causes the request token bucket to hit quota_exceeded rapidly. On top of that, our autoscaling for dedicated fallback was delayed due to a parallel capacity guardrail that prevented creating new dedicated workers for tenants flagged as "standard". Net effect: sustained 429s and increased queueing leading to higher p95s.

Metrics observed (internal):
- 429s peaked at 18% for 00:15–00:45 UTC on 2026-08-19.
- p95 latency pre-change: ~120ms; post-change: ~380ms.
- Throughput drop ~40% for OptiDocs requests.

Immediate mitigations to apply (recommended order):
1) Roll back the burst-window rule for OptiDocs (targeted flag flip) — quickest revert.
2) Temporarily increase per-tenant burst credits for OptiDocs by 3x for 2 hours.
3) Bypass the standard capacity guardrail for OptiDocs and allow dedicated fallback pool to spin up (manual override).
4) If rollback isn't immediate, route OptiDocs traffic to the dedicated pool (connor to coordinate).

I can implement steps 1+2 within 15 minutes if we have exec approval to proceed.

Please confirm and I'll authorize Sean to apply the changes now.

Attached is a short MAP (updated_MAP_OptiDocs.docx) with timelines and asks for the postmortem (quota rule targeting fix, better rollout gating, and guaranteed dedicated-fallback for enterprise tier). OptiDocs requests a follow-up with engineering and product next week to review the postmortem and the customer credit proposal.

We'll stand by for the postmortem and the formal credit offer. Thank you for the rapid triage and transparency.

Regards,
Alex Tan
